CV03-q01-0kbm24: Positioning the tractor is Step 3; first you inspect the fifth wheel, then the area.
Connecting the air lines is Step 7; the first step is inspecting the fifth wheel.
CV03-q02-940qpg: Level is what some websites say; the handbook wants it tilted down toward the rear, jaws open.
The tilt is down toward the rear of the tractor, not the cab, so the trailer can ride up onto it.
CV03-q03-q5swjj: Too high and the trailer may not couple correctly; the tractor should lift it slightly.
Level isn't the target; the trailer should be low enough that the tractor raises it slightly.
CV03-q04-0qht5m: Not coupling correctly is the risk when the trailer is too high, not too low.
Landing gear lifting isn't the handbook's warning; too low means the tractor may hit the nose.
CV03-q05-bmfgx5: Backing under is Step 10; air lines, air supply and locking the trailer brakes come first.
Raising the landing gear is Step 15, after the coupling is made and inspected.
CV03-q06-nyxo5s: Air escapes when you release the brakes; when you apply them, you hear the brakes move.
You're listening for the brakes, not a buzzer: brakes moving on apply, air escaping on release.
CV03-q07-3lq272: Pushing the knob in releases the trailer brakes; lock them so the trailer stays put as you back under.
The chocks stay on until the very last step of coupling.
CV03-q08-pbpvk6: The tug test pulls forward gently with the trailer brakes locked; don't release them or back firmly.
Never drive with the landing gear down; the tug test is a gentle pull with the gear slightly raised.
CV03-q09-0oh1ag: The key isn't about the parking brakes; you take it so nobody moves the truck while you're under it.
The battery isn't the reason; taking the key keeps anyone from moving the truck while you're under it.
CV03-q10-d4ae10: Grease prevents steering friction; a gap between the plates warns the kingpin may be on top of closed jaws.
Front loading isn't the concern; any gap may mean the kingpin is resting on top of closed jaws.
CV03-q11-wcpjed: Checking that the locking lever is in "lock" is part of the coupling inspection.
Checking that the safety latch is over the locking lever is part of the coupling inspection.
CV03-q12-59tpql: The handbook's checks are tractor frame to landing gear, and tractor tires to trailer nose.
Glad hands and kingpin aren't the clearance check; check tractor frame to landing gear.
CV03-q13-fitjb4: Raising the landing gear is Step 15; removing the chocks comes after it.
The electrical cord is Step 14; the last step is removing and storing the chocks.
CV03-q14-uv5sq6: Pulling forward keeps pressure on the jaws; back up gently to ease it.
Unlocking the fifth wheel comes later; first ease the pressure on the jaws and set the parking brakes.
CV03-q15-z1b9j0: Those emergency brakes run on tank air that can leak away; if unsure, chock the wheels.
Chock whenever there are no spring brakes or you're unsure, hill or not.
CV03-q16-azggx3: With a loaded trailer, give a few extra turns in low gear to take weight off the tractor.
Never lift the trailer off the fifth wheel; just a few extra turns in low gear.
CV03-q17-npwtwf: Stop first with the frame still under the trailer, so it catches the trailer if the landing gear fails.

CV03-q18-hfuqh3: A locked pintle hook has the handle turned up flush with the top of the latch, not hanging down.
A fully upright latch is the open position you set before lowering the drawbar eye on.
CV03-dn-fpsbaw: 10 is the number of uncoupling steps.
7 isn't the count; coupling has 16 steps and uncoupling has 10.
CV03-dn-g5b3ux: Inspecting the fifth wheel comes first, not third; backing slowly is Step 4.
Air lines are Step 7 and backing under is Step 10; the first step is inspecting the fifth wheel.
CV03-dn-rftgc3: Level is what some websites say; the handbook wants it tilted down toward the rear.
The jaws must be open and a sliding fifth wheel locked, not jaws closed and slider unlocked.
CV03-dn-i1dnwz: Hitting and damaging the nose is what happens when the trailer is too low.

CV03-dn-i2aj0a: The electrical cord and raising the landing gear come after coupling, at Steps 14 and 15.
Air lines, the brake check and locking the trailer brakes (Steps 7–9) come before backing under.

It isn't about saving air; engine off lets you hear the brakes apply and release.

Rolling back in neutral isn't the method; back slowly in the lowest reverse gear.

Raise the landing gear slightly off the ground and keep the trailer brakes locked.
CV03-dn-6avddx: Any gap may mean the kingpin sits on top of closed jaws; there must be no space.
0.3–0.5 mm is the ball-type drawbar clearance, not the fifth-wheel gap.
CV03-dn-3phg8z: The head is the bottom end of the kingpin; the jaws close around the shank.
The top plate is the trailer's upper fifth wheel; the jaws close around the kingpin shank.
CV03-dn-2s3xii: Just off the pavement isn't enough; gear left partway up can catch on railroad tracks.
Never drive with it halfway; raise it all the way up and secure the crank handle.
CV03-dn-z0b2e2: Plug up can let moisture in; hang the cable with the plug down.
Glad hands go on the dummy couplers; the cable hangs plug down to keep moisture out.
CV03-dn-hkhsq1: Hand-tight isn't enough; both lock screws are torqued to 350–400 Nm.
0.3–0.5 is the vertical clearance in millimeters, not a torque.
CV03-dn-4ritvs: Not just goosenecks; by law every trailer must have safety chains.
Brakes don't matter; by law every trailer must have safety chains.
